title: S. Koreans in Their 60s and 70s Don't Feel Old — Survey
paragraphs: People often say: "You're only as old as you feel!"
And a new survey in South Korea has found that many people who are retired or almost retired don't feel old at all!
More than 500 people took part in the survey. They were all between 60 and 74 years old.
Almost 76% of survey participants said they don't think of themselves as old. And that went above 80% for people in their 60s.
The participants were also asked questions about what it means to be old.
Many said that if you can do everyday activities, you're not old. Others also said that having good health means you're not old.
Sometimes, we may think of older people as needing help. But the survey found that many older people in South Korea still want to help others.
And about two-thirds said that older people should have more chances to help others by sharing what they know.
Fifty-two percent also said they would like to learn something new.
A different survey found that one in five people in South Korea are now 65 or older. By 2036, 30% of people in the country could be 65 or older — and that could go up to 40% by 2050.
So, with more people getting older, maybe it's time to think differently about what it means to be old!
